items.title: Trump singles out Australia as he criticises allies on Iran war support
items.description: The US president singles out Australia as a country he was surprised was unwilling to help secure the Strait of Hormuz amid the war with Iran.

items.title: Trump reveals Iran's 'great gift', plus what else you should know this morning
items.description: Mr Trump is now sceptical at the prospect of a peace deal soon, just days after saying there were positive signs for peace. Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran has your daily update on the Middle East conflict.

items.title: Is the end of the Iran war near?
items.description: Donald Trump says Iran wants a ceasefire deal. But Tehran says it's not even talking with the US. So what's going on and how likely is a ceasefire?

items.title: Live: Trump extends deadline for Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: US President Donald Trump extends his deadline for Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz, saying he will hold off on bombing Iran's energy plants. Earlier, an Iranian official called US proposals for a ceasefire "one-sided and unfair". Follow live.

items.title: Live: 'Monster' Cyclone Narelle to cross WA coast later today
items.description: The storm, which has already made landfall in Far North Queensland and the Northern Territory, is now impacting the west Pilbara coast.

items.title: Live: Marles defends Australia's Middle East contribution after Trump's comments
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles has defended Australia's contribution to the defence of Gulf states after US President Donald Trump's comments. Follow live.

items.title: Superannuation giant HESTA's new admin provider on brink of collapse
items.description: Experts are concerned one of Australia's largest super funds has invested in a new admin company whose most recent financial report indicates it is insolvent.

items.title: IOC bans transgender athletes from women's events
items.description: Under changes announced by the International Olympic Committee, the gender of athletes will be determined by a one-time gene-screening test.

items.title: Australian dependence on imported packaging exposed by Iran war
items.description: The war in Iran renews the government's interest in reducing Australia's dependence on imported packaging, particularly oil-reliant plastic.

items.title: Katherine's worst flood in 28 years leaves survivors with disaster 'PTSD'
items.description: As it recovers from its worst flooding in decades, those living in the NT town of Katherine are trying to come to terms with the ongoing threat on their doorstep.

items.title: 'There is still hope': Former detective reflects six months on from Gus's disappearance
items.description: Six months to the day since four-year-old Gus Lamont was reported missing from a vast outback station, many more questions than answers remain.

items.title: Fuel not the only political problem posed by Middle East war
items.description: Fuel prices are the immediate issue for the Albanese government but it will also be under scrutiny for how it handles Australia's relationship with the United States and its volatile president.

items.title: Soaring diesel prices hit roads, housing and infrastructure builds
items.description: Industry groups have warned some infrastructure projects could stall without additional government support to cover fuel-related costs.

items.title: 'Reliable evidence': Exercise halves early death risk of middle-aged women
items.description: Australian researchers found that middle-aged women who exercised regularly halved their risk of premature death. But most women aren't meeting physical activity guidelines.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Jet fuel shortages, headbutting whales and Donald Trump's social faux pas
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: Grey's Anatomy marks 21 years of love, loss and disasters
items.description: Twenty-one years ago today, a group of interns walked into the fictional Seattle Grace Hospital to start their surgical careers. It was the start of the longest-running medical drama in US TV history.

items.title: Nazeem Hussain developed his 'gut-punch' comedy over a lifetime of racism
items.description: For comedian Nazeem Hussain, the best way to respond to war, discrimination and racism is to laugh about it. And he's built his whole career on this special brand of risky, outrageous comedy.

items.title: Craig's experience of abuse is not uncommon — but it is seldom talked about
items.description: Craig Hughes-Cashmore spent more than 20 years living with persistent suicidal thoughts, an experience that many share but rarely feel able to discuss.

items.title: Complaints about foul smells skyrocket in Melbourne's west
items.description: Adam Pattison spent two years doing up his backyard to enjoy outdoor barbecues, but says "sickening" smells kill the vibe five times a week.

items.title: Severe storm causes thousands of power outages, knocks out transport
items.description: Fire and Rescue NSW says there has been more than 400 calls for help, including one incident where a tree fell on a house trapping the occupant.

items.title: Petition calls for video of death in custody to be released despite coroner ruling
items.description: Raylene Nixon says the public should be able to make their own minds up about what happened to her son in his final moments.

items.title: ASIC expands in NT after investigation into Indigenous customers' bank fees
items.description: The chair of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission says the expansion of the watchdog agency in Darwin will help the organisation better enforce regulations in remote communities.

items.title: The One Nation vote in SA
items.description: One Nation just sent a shiver through the Liberal Party, after a breakthrough result in South Australia.  Pauline Hanson's party achieved more than 21 per cent of the statewide primary vote, beating the Liberal Party and becoming the second-highest polling party. But nationally, more attention has been on the undercard fight, and that has left the Liberal Party deeply wounded.

items.title: More than 250 voters in Coober Pedy unable to have their say in SA election
items.description: Nearly one in three Coober Pedy voters, or more than 250 people, missed their chance to vote in the state election last week after the town was left without a polling booth on election day.

items.title: Second 'crew' charged over Sydney woman's kidnapping, murder
items.description: Further charges have been laid over the alleged kidnapping and murder of a western Sydney woman who police believe was targeted due to her husband's organised crime links.
